title: Genesis close
hookLine: from a garden to a family in Egypt: God keeps promises through broken people
last: FEAR NOT, I WILL NOURISH YOU.

cards: Genesis opens with the whole universe: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." Light, oceans, stars, a garden, two people.
Fifty chapters later, it closes on a single box: "So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt." From the heavens to a coffin.
If you read it as a story about people getting things right, it's a strange ending. But Genesis was never that story. For forty-five days we've walked through it together.
Today, the whole book in one look.

teach.h: A GARDEN, A QUESTION, A FLOOD.
teach.b: It began with light and good and very good, with dust that had breath in it, and a garden to tend and keep. Then a serpent's question, and God walking in the cool of the day asking, where are you?
Coats of skins, made by God, for people who had just disobeyed. Cain and Abel, and being your brother's keeper. Noah building anyway, a dove with an olive leaf, a rainbow that said never again.
Babel, where people tried to make a name for themselves. Then one family. Abraham told to go, not knowing where.
Stars to count. Hagar, a slave woman, naming the God who sees her. Strangers at Mamre, and Sarah laughing.
Abraham arguing with God for a city. Isaac, laughter. A ram on Moriah.

Chesed, Esau and a bowl of stew, Jacob in goat skins, a stairway at Bethel, a wrestling match by a river, a brother who ran. And Joseph: a coat, a pit, a prison, and I am your brother. Look at the people.
Liars, schemers, favorites, runaways, brothers who sold a brother. Not one is a saint throughout.
And yet the promise God made to Abraham, a family through whom all the families of the earth would be blessed, still stands on the last page.
Broken people, kept promises. And Genesis ends leaning forward.
Joseph's last words: God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land; carry my bones with you.
Christians and Jews both read Genesis as the beginning, not the whole. The coffin waits for a journey.

how: Christians read Genesis as the opening of the whole biblical story; reading plans that go through the Bible in order begin here and run straight on into Exodus.

games.q: you're Joseph, a hundred and ten, dying in Egypt. your family is safe and fed here. what do you ask of your brothers?
o: bury me here, in Egypt, where I lived.
when God brings you out, carry my bones with you.
never leave Egypt; it saved us.
games.why: he makes them swear: God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence. Genesis ends waiting for a journey.

practice: Call up your family, the one you were born into or the one you've made, with its favorites and feuds: not the polished version, the real one. Find one sentence that holds something true about it, and write it down if you can.
If you pray, you can offer that sentence to God; if you don't, just keep it.

wordCard.voice: Genesis close. The end of the book of beginnings: from creation to a family in Egypt, held together by God's promise to Abraham.

orig.note: Hebrew: in the beginning. the book's first word, and its name in Hebrew.
